programme.title: Munro: Mountain Man
programme.desc: Little more than 100 years ago, Scottish mountains standing at more than 3,000 feet were virtually unknown. Today they are familiar terrain to many thousands of climbers, thanks to Victorian adventurer Hugh Munro's determination to list the high peaks which now define the Highlands and Islands of Scotland. Nicholas Crane tells the story of the magnificent peaks that bear his name.

programme.title: Strauss: The Waltz King
programme.desc: The original `dirty dancing' became a century-long craze, but behind it was a bitter tale of father and son rivalry. The music of the time is played by the Wiener Akademie orchestra in Vienna's sumptuous Hofburg Palace.

programme.title: Around the World in 80 Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don continues his journey with a visit to the richest and most powerful nation in the world: the United States of America. There, he meets garden guerrillas in New York, visits a Virginian garden that reflects the birth of the nation, and finally travels west to California, to see if gardens there reflect more than the glitz of the movie industry.

programme.title: Henry VIII: Patron or Plunderer?
programme.desc: In the 1530s, King Henry VIII was at a crossroads. In his desperation for a new wife and an heir, he had broken with Rome, divorced Katherine of Aragon and married Anne Boleyn. Isolated and vulnerable, he needed a powerful new image as head of church and state. Jonathan Foyle looks for clues in the king's art to glimpse what was going on inside Henry's head as he faced his darkest days.

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: Three, two, one, lift off! This edition launches into the extraordinary - and extraterrestrial - world of astronaut training, discovering what it truly takes to become a European Space Agency (ESA) astronaut. As Europe looks to play a more prominent role in space exploration, we shine a spotlight on the candidates who are pushing boundaries and preparing to represent Great Britain and Northern Ireland amongst the stars.

programme.title: The Great Philosophers
programme.desc: Myles Burnyeat looks at Plato, the first western philosopher whose written works have survived.

programme.title: The Great Philosophers
programme.desc: Martha Nussbaum presents a programme about Aristotle, Plato's star pupil and tutor to the young Alexander the Great. His philosophy dominated western thought for many hundreds of years and is still studied at every university.

programme.title: The Great Philosophers

programme.title: The Channel Tunnel: Life on the Inside

programme.title: The Good Life
programme.desc: The Goods decide to try their needles at making their own clothes. Meanwhile, Jerry is jockeying for the position of managing director of JJM, with Margo providing some Machiavellian assistance.

programme.title: Yes, Prime Minister
programme.desc: Hacker prepares to make his first broadcast as prime minister, announcing his grand new defence policy, but finds it is not so easy to speak on camera.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Robert Robinson hosts a game of word definitions and deceptions. Captains Frank Muir and Patrick Campbell are joined by Tom Baker, Alan Coren, Gabrielle Drake and Miriam Stoppard.

programme.title: Face the Music
programme.desc: Joseph Cooper invites viewers to match their musical wits against Judith Jackson, Robin Ray and Patrick Moore. With guest musician Louis Kentner.

programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: When Russia invades Ukraine, a quiet schoolteacher picks up his camera and becomes an unlikely dissident. What emerges is a chilling portrait of how propaganda seeps into everyday life and how even children are drawn into the machinery of war.

programme.title: Blood and Gold: The Making of Spain with Simon Sebag Montefiore
programme.desc: Simon uncovers the truth about Spain's hero El Cid. He also investigates the horror of the Spanish Inquisition and in the process discovers an unsettling story about one of his own ancestors.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.sub-title: How to Write a Mills and Boon
programme.desc: To mark 100 years of romance publishers Mills and Boon, literary novelist Stella Duffy takes on the challenge of writing for them. Romantic fiction is a global phenomenon, and Mills and Boon are among the biggest names in the business. The company welcomes submissions from new authors, but as Duffy soon finds out, writing a Mills and Boon is harder than it looks.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Building of Britain
programme.desc: Fred Dibnah takes his series on the building of Britain to his home turf, Lancashire, so he can wax lyrical over the roots of the nation's canal network. He visits Worsley to see where it all began and, in his own back garden, and demonstrates the early canal-building process. Fred then takes a trip on the Leeds-Liverpool waterway, revealing the hard work and skill that made such a passage possible.

programme.title: Archaeology: A Secret History
programme.desc: Archaeologist Richard Miles presents a series charting the history of the breakthroughs and watersheds in our long quest to understand our ancient past. He begins by going back 2,000 years to explore how archaeology began by trying to prove a biblical truth - a quest that soon got archaeologists into dangerous water.

programme.title: Thatcher: A Very British Revolution
programme.desc: Mrs Thatcher plunged into dramatic conflicts that defined her premiership and her legacy. Against a backdrop of economic downturn Mrs Thatcher struggled in the opinion polls and was labelled the `least popular Prime Minister since polling began' but her public image was be transformed by a totally unexpected turn of events in the South Atlantic.

programme.title: The Falklands Play
programme.desc: The British prime minister must deal with a diplomatic breakdown when an undeclared war breaks out between Britain and Argentina to regain the Falkland Islands.

programme.title: How to Get Ahead
programme.desc: Stephen Smith, explores Renaissance Florence under the reign of Grand Duke Cosimo Medici. Cosimo's fledgling court prized the finer things in life and some of the greatest painters, sculptors and craftsmen in world history came to serve the Grand Duke. However, successful courtiers had to have brains as well as brawn. The canniest of them looked to theorists like Niccolo Machiavelli for underhand ways to get ahead, whilst enlightened polymaths turned their minds to the heavens, and to ice cream.
